open_questions: His own account of his parts in Inside Out (2004), not read here; the interviews read are Far Out's (2024) and The Drummer's Journal's (2014).
His kits record by record: the Songsterr track names (Premier, Ludwig, Ludwig Cortex Maple Custom, DW) are the transcribers' labels; Wikipedia gives Premier, then Ludwig, then DW.
Whether a kick sits under Astronomy Domine's floor tom: the tab writes none.
Dogs' first guitar solo has Gilmour's tom overdubs (the album credits him); the tab gives them a track of their own, not read.
The Final Cut, A Momentary Lapse of Reason, The Division Bell and The Endless River are not in the style; nor are the guitar solos of Money and Have a Cigar, or Shine On Parts VI to IX.

identity.name: Nick Mason
identity.summary: Pink Floyd's drummer from the band's first days to its last, the only member on every album: a light, laid-back player who left the band room, the hats or ride in eighths over a plain 2 and 4, half time with the snare on 3, the meter turned with the riff (Money's 7/4, Have a Cigar's 5/4), and the toms as a voice of their own, from Astronomy Domine's floor tom to the roto-toms of Time.

institutions.name: Regent Street Polytechnic (now the University of Westminster)
institutions.outcome: Studied architecture, 1962 to 1967, and formed Sigma 6 there with Roger Waters, Bob Klose and Richard Wright, the band that became Pink Floyd.

traditions.impact: 'Influenced by jazz and big band music' (Wikipedia); in Mitch Mitchell, 'something very jazzy ... holding things back and playing slightly behind'.

traditions.tradition: British blues and rock drummers of the 1960s
traditions.impact: Ginger Baker's two bass drums and mallets; Mitch Mitchell's light feel. 'I was influenced by everyone who was around at that time.'

formative_events.event: Formed Sigma 6 at the Regent Street Polytechnic with Roger Waters, Bob Klose and Richard Wright.
The Piper at the Gates of Dawn, under Syd Barrett.
The Dark Side of the Moon: the roto-toms on Time and the heartbeat bass drum.
Formed Nick Mason's Saucerful of Secrets to play the band's early music.

eras.label: The Barrett years
eras.context: Under Syd Barrett, on a Premier kit: psychedelic songs, the toms carrying them.

eras.label: Meddle and Pompeii
eras.context: Ludwig drums and two bass drums after Ginger Baker; long pieces, improvised live; Live at Pompeii.
defining_traits: the crash ridden on the beat

eras.label: The Dark Side of the Moon to The Wall
eras.context: The concept albums: a damped studio kit, roto-toms, half time, the meter turned with the riff; on The Wall, Bob Ezrin's disco beat.

eras.label: Later years
eras.context: With Gilmour and Wright from 1987, then his own band, Nick Mason's Saucerful of Secrets, from 2018, on a DW double bass kit.

swing.notes: Straight; Shine On and One of These Days carry triplets in places.

dynamics.balance: Light and even; no ghost notes in the tabs read; the snare fatter and gentler from Echoes on (Wikipedia).

feel_profile.interaction: Under the song: the kick with the bass, the groove left plain under long guitar and keyboard solos.

hand_techniques.name: half time
hand_techniques.description: The snare on 3 alone under the hats or ride on the beat (Time, Have a Cigar, the Minimoog solo of Dogs).

hand_techniques.name: the toms as the groove
hand_techniques.description: Astronomy Domine's floor tom in eighths, One of These Days' toms galloping in triplets with the bass, Time's roto-tom solo.

hand_techniques.name: the crash ridden on the beat
hand_techniques.description: One of These Days' two crashes in turn on every beat.

foot_techniques.name: four on the floor
foot_techniques.description: Another Brick in the Wall, Part 2's kick on every beat, at Bob Ezrin's suggestion.

foot_techniques.name: the heartbeat
foot_techniques.description: A treated bass drum on 1 and its "and", a heartbeat, under Time's intro (and Speak to Me, On the Run and Eclipse).

devices.description: Dogs: 'the tempo is cut in half' into the middle section in 6/8, the old quarter becoming the new eighth (the tab's 4/4 at 105 to 6/8 at 52; the record's eighth there at 104.7).

evidence.note: Wikipedia says the tempo is cut in half; the ratio, quarter to eighth, is the tab's and the measurement's.

searched: The ten Songsterr tabs read section by section (Astronomy Domine to Comfortably Numb)
Wikipedia on him and on each song (Money's 7/4, Shine On's 6/8 to 12/8, Dogs' halved tempo, Mother's meters)
Far Out's 2024 interview and The Drummer's Journal's 2014 interview
devices_search.note: One device, Dogs' metric modulation. The meters (Money's 7/4, Have a Cigar's 5/4, 2/4 and 3/4, Shine On's 6/4) are written as sections in their own meters, not as devices. Shine On's switch from 6/8 to 12/8 regroups the same bar (Wikipedia: 'the feeling that the tempo doubles up'); the tempo does not change, so it is not counted as a modulation.

voice_language.snare: A plain 2 and 4, or 3 alone in half time; from Echoes on fatter and gentler (Wikipedia).
voice_language.kick: With the bass: on 1 and the "and" of 2, on the "a" of 2, four on the floor for The Wall; a heartbeat under Time.
voice_language.toms: A voice of their own: the floor tom in eighths, triplet gallops, roto-tom melodies; fills down the toms at a phrase's end.
voice_language.hihat: Eighths, opened on the "and" of 4; on the beat in half time.
voice_language.ride: Eighths under the guitar solos; on the beat in half time.
voice_language.cymbals: Paiste: a crash on 1 of a phrase; two crashes ridden in turn on One of These Days.

aesthetic: damped and dry on the 1970s albums
sound_profile.cymbal_character: Paiste throughout his career with Pink Floyd (Wikipedia); Formula 602 named by the Money tab.

by_era.description: A Premier kit at Abbey Road, the toms ringing.
A damped Ludwig, dry and close, mixed "dry" and "clean" at his and Waters' wish on The Dark Side of the Moon; roto-toms on Time.

sample_hints.1967: Sixties Ludwig: ringing toms and a bright snare.
sample_hints.1971: SM Drums: a 1960s Ludwig, round and warm.
sample_hints.1973-1977: Damped and dead: a damped kick and deadened toms.
sample_hints.1979: Studio rock: tight, dry and close.

signature_traits.label: Half time, the snare on 3
signature_traits.description: The hats or ride on the beat and the snare on 3 alone, the kick round it (Time, Have a Cigar).

signature_traits.label: The toms as a voice
signature_traits.description: The floor tom in eighths through Astronomy Domine, the toms galloping in One of These Days, the roto-tom solo in Time.

signature_traits.label: The meter turned with the riff
signature_traits.description: Money's 7/4 with its chorus in 4/4 and 6/4; Have a Cigar's chorus through 5/4, 2/4 and 3/4; Shine On in 6/4.

signature_traits.label: Space under the solos
signature_traits.description: Plain bars left plain for long guitar and keyboard solos: Time's chorus with nothing but the kick on 1 and 2 and the snare on 3.

patterns.name: Astronomy Domine: the floor tom in eighths
patterns.function: The floor tom on every eighth of the 12/8 bar under a crash on 1; no snare and no kick in the tab

patterns.name: Astronomy Domine: the rack tom answers
patterns.function: The floor tom in eighths, the rack tom answering from the "and" of the third pulse

patterns.name: One of These Days: the toms galloping in triplets
patterns.function: The floor tom twice and the mid tom on 1 and 3, the kick on the second triplet of 2 and 4, the hat foot on the beat, with the bass

evidence.note: The tab counts the song at 120 and 126; the record runs at 135 to 140.

patterns.name: One of These Days: the crash ridden on the beat
patterns.function: Two crashes in turn on the beat, the first on the "and" of 4, over the snare on 2 and 4 and the kick on 1 and 3

patterns.name: Echoes: the verse
patterns.function: The ride in eighths with sixteenths on the "and" and "a" of 2 and 4, the kick on 1, the "a" of 2, 3 and the "a" of 4

patterns.name: Echoes: the funk jam
patterns.function: The hats in sixteenths round the beat, a crash on 2, the kick round the bass

patterns.name: Time: the roto-toms over the heartbeat
patterns.function: The kick on 1 and its "and", a heartbeat, and the roto-toms answering in sixteenth-note triplets

evidence.note: The transcriber wrote the four roto-toms as bongos and congas; here high to low on the toms. The BeatBreaker song writes each run of three into the beat as two.

patterns.name: Time: the verse in half time
patterns.function: A crash on 1, the hats on 2 to 4, the snare on 3 alone, the kick on 1 and the "and"s of 2, 3 and 4

patterns.name: Time: the chorus
patterns.function: Nothing but the kick on 1 and 2 and the snare on 3

patterns.name: Money: the verse in 7/4
patterns.function: The crash on 1 and 7, the hats on 2 to 6, the snare on 2, 4 and 6, the kick on 1, 3, its "and", 5 and 7

patterns.name: Money: the chorus's bar of 6/4
patterns.function: The chorus's third bar: the crash on 1, the hats on 2 to 6, the snare on 2, 4 and 6

patterns.name: Have a Cigar: the intro in half time
patterns.function: The hats on the beat, the snare on 3, the kick on 1, the "and" of 2 and the "and" of 4

patterns.name: Have a Cigar: the verse
patterns.function: The ride on the beat, the snare on the "and" of 1 and on 3

patterns.name: Have a Cigar: the chorus's bar of 5/4
patterns.function: The crash and kick on 2, the ride on 3 to 5, the snare on 4

patterns.name: Shine On You Crazy Diamond: Part II
patterns.function: The ride on every beat of 6/4, one backbeat on 4, the kick on 1 and into 6

evidence.note: The kick before 6 is the last triplet of 5 in the tab, written on the "a" of 5.

patterns.name: Shine On You Crazy Diamond: the end of Part V in twelve
patterns.function: The same bar counted in four dotted quarters: the hats on the pulse, the snare on the second and fourth

patterns.name: Dogs: the verse
patterns.function: The ride in eighths, the snare on 2 and 4, the kick on 1 and the "and" of 2

patterns.name: Dogs: the middle in 6/8
patterns.function: Half the tempo: the ride in eighths, the kick on 1, no snare

patterns.name: Another Brick in the Wall, Part 2: four on the floor
patterns.function: The kick on every beat, the hats in eighths opened on the "and" of 4, the snare on 2 and 4

patterns.name: Another Brick in the Wall, Part 2: the guitar solo
patterns.function: The kick on every beat, the hats in eighths, the snare on 4 alone

patterns.name: Comfortably Numb: the verse
patterns.function: The hats in eighths over a plain 2 and 4, the kick on 1 and 3

patterns.name: Comfortably Numb: the chorus and solos
patterns.function: The second crash on 1, the ride in eighths, the kick on 1, the "a" of 2 and 3

equipment.label: Ludwig kits, two bass drums at Pompeii, Paiste cymbals
equipment.layout_notes: Wikipedia: Premier drums at first, Ludwig after seeing Ginger Baker use them, briefly Fibes, then Drum Workshop; Paiste cymbals throughout; Remo heads, and Remo roto-toms on Time. At Pompeii in 1971 a silver sparkle Ludwig with two bass drums, their front heads painted with mandalas, and a gong behind.

affiliations.name: Pink Floyd
affiliations.notes: A founder; the only constant member and the only one on every album.

affiliations.name: Nick Mason's Saucerful of Secrets
affiliations.notes: His own band, playing Pink Floyd's early music.

evidence.note: 'Ginger was a huge influence on me actually getting a bit more serious about playing and being in a band'; 'the whole double bass drum thing completely bowled me over' (Far Out, 2024). He changed from Premier to Ludwig drums after seeing Baker use them (Wikipedia).
'He was a sort of mentor for me and I loved his style ... that thing of holding things back and playing slightly behind ... that light feel that he had' (Far Out, 2024).
Portnoy, guest editor of Rhythm in January 2007, chose him among the four drummers 'that shaped me in my early formative years', with Bruford, Ulrich and Peart, and interviewed him.
On The Wall (1979): Porcaro drums on Mother, whose changing meters Mason found hard to learn on a tight schedule; Mason on the rest.
From Sigma 6 at the Regent Street Polytechnic to Waters' leaving in 1985; the rhythm section that laid Shine On down first.
From 1968 to the end of the band.
From Sigma 6 to Wright's death in 2008.

philosophy.idea: Not overplaying: the tendency is to play more and faster, and the work is controlling it.
His own style came from not having lessons; he would not have played the way he did with them.

innovations: Roto-toms as a melodic voice on a rock record (Time, 1973)
Progressive rock drumming that left space: half time and plain bars under long solos

cultural_references.description: The only member of Pink Floyd on every one of its albums.
Rock and Roll Hall of Fame with Pink Floyd, 1996.

common_misconceptions: That he drums on all of The Wall: Jeff Porcaro plays Mother.

beatbreaker.default_kit_sound: A damped 1970s kit, short and dark; a ringing 1960s Ludwig for the early songs; tight and dry for The Wall
generation_rules: The hats or ride in eighths over a plain 2 and 4, the kick on 1 and the "and" of 2.
Half time: the snare on 3 alone, the hats or ride on the beat.
Meters in sections of their own, the groove kept plain through each.
The toms as the groove: the floor tom in eighths, triplet gallops, roto-tom phrases.

lineage_display.lineage_blurb: Ginger Baker's two bass drums and Mitch Mitchell's light feel, then Pink Floyd for fifty years; Mike Portnoy named him among the drummers who shaped him.
